newsitem.title: USA: Ariz. Salt River Project set Mon cutoff for tender.
newsitem.headline: Ariz. Salt River Project set Mon cutoff for tender.

text.p: Responses to the Salt River Project's (SRP) solicitation to acquire power between Jun 15 and Sept 15, for each year from 1998 to 2006, are due next Monday, the Arizona-based public utility said Tuesday.

The solicitation noted that SRP aims to develop one or more arrangements that will result in an acceptable exchange of products and/or services of equivalent value, not necessarily an exchange of equivalent kilowatt hours.
SRP sees highest demand in the summer, with daily peaks in mid-afternoon. But from October to May, peak demand is in the morning, and surplus energy is available throughout the day.
"We are looking for someone who has a seasonal load to complement ours," said Joanne Itow, senior planning analyst at SRP.
The utility is interested in proposals at minimum increments of 25 megawatts (MW), up to a maximum of 500 MW from each potential supplier for each year.
SRP said it plans to evaluate responses to the solicitation by the end of the year.
Earlier this month, SRP announced an alliance with Tenaska Power Services Co and Canada's Powerex to market wholesale electric power throughout western North America.
Itow noted that the alliance, under which SRP will make 300 MW of power available during the winter season, is a way for all partners to "find markets for excess supplies."
